[LLM] Python process executing transformers.pyz dropped from git-tanstack.com (TeamPCP) Installation High
Hunts the post-import dropper stage: a python interpreter invoked with the staged payload filename `transformers.pyz` or writing that file to disk. This is the second-stage execution from the malicious guardrails-ai 0.10.1 __init__.py and is shared with the broader TanStack/Mistral mini-Shai-Hulud campaign. Rationale: SafeDep + Qualys reverse-engineered the malicious `guardrails/__init__.py` and identified the exact dropper filename `transformers.pyz` pulled from git-tanstack.com and executed via python3. `.pyz` is a Python zipapp — a high-signal extension on a process command line because legitimate transformers (HuggingFace) ships as a wheel, not a zipapp. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/ • https://qualysec.com/cybersecurity-news/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-170-packages-hit-across-npm-pypi/
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.006 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem

union isfuzzy=true
(

  | where FileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","python","python3")
     or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","python","python3")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "transformers.pyz"
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "transformers.pyz"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, ActionType="ProcessCreate"
),
(
  DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where FileName =~ "transformers.pyz"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, ActionType
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 30d;
union isfuzzy=true
(
  ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","pythonw")
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "transformers.pyz"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, ProcessName=ActingProcessName, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, Source="ImProcessCreate"
),

),

description: Detects a python interpreter invoked with the second-stage payload filename transformers.pyz used by the TeamPCP supply-chain campaign behind the malicious guardrails-ai 0.10.1 PyPI release (CVE-2026-45758) and the parallel TanStack/Mistral npm compromises.
references:

[LLM] DNS lookup for git-tanstack.com TeamPCP C2 staging domain Command & Control High
Detects any DNS query for the attacker-controlled domain git-tanstack.com used to host the transformers.pyz second-stage payload in the guardrails-ai 0.10.1 (CVE-2026-45758) and parallel TanStack/Mistral mini-Shai-Hulud campaign. Rationale: git-tanstack.com is the exact attacker domain identified by SafeDep, Qualys and Ox Security as the staging host for the TeamPCP campaign's transformers.pyz payload — the name typosquats the legitimate TanStack open-source org. Any successful resolution from inside the enterprise indicates either active compromise or sandbox detonation. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/ • https://qualysec.com/cybersecurity-news/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-170-packages-hit-across-npm-pypi/
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
let LookbackDays = 30d;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemoteUrl has "git-tanstack.com" or RemoteIP == "83.142.209.194"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 30d;
union isfuzzy=true
(
  DnsEvents

  | where Name has "git-tanstack.com"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Query=Name, QueryType, Source="DnsEvents"
),
(
  ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where DnsQuery has "git-tanstack.com"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Query=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, Source="ImDnsActivity"
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where DestinationHostName has "git-tanstack.com" or RequestURL has "git-tanstack.com"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP=SourceIP, Query=coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), QueryType="WebProxy", Source="CommonSecurityLog"
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Outbound connection to TeamPCP C2 IP 83.142.209.194 Command & Control High
Detects any TCP/UDP connection to the attacker-controlled IP 83.142.209.194 hosting git-tanstack.com and the transformers.pyz dropper. Catches DNS-bypass / direct-IP fetches and proxy-tunnelled connections the DNS UC would miss. Rationale: 83.142.209.194 is the canonical IP for git-tanstack.com identified in the pre-extracted IOC bundle and confirmed by the SafeDep + Qualys writeups of the TeamPCP campaign. Direct-IP detection catches dropper variants that hard-code the IP to bypass DNS-based blocks. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/ • https://qualysec.com/cybersecurity-news/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises/

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol, LocalIP, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc

let C2IP = "83.142.209.194";
union isfuzzy=true
(

  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where DestinationIP == C2IP
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, Source="CommonSecurityLog"
),
(
  ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where DstIpAddr == C2IP
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, DestinationIP=DstIpAddr, DestinationPort=DstPortNumber, RequestURL=Url, DeviceVendor=EventVendor, DeviceProduct=EventProduct, Source="ImNetworkSession"
),
(
  AzureDiagnostics
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where ResourceType =~ "AZUREFIREWALLS" or Category has "FirewallDnatRule" or Category has "FirewallApplicationRule" or Category has "FirewallNetworkRule"
  | where Properties has C2IP
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=Resource, SourceIP=tostring(""), DestinationIP=C2IP, DestinationPort=tostring(""), RequestURL=tostring(Properties), DeviceVendor="Microsoft", DeviceProduct="AzureFirewall", Source="AzureDiagnostics"
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45758")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45758")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation

    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.

[LLM] GlassFish java process spawning command shell (CVE-2026-2587 RCE) Exploitation High
Detects the GlassFish admin console java process spawning a command interpreter or LOLBin child — the post-exploitation pivot after EL injection via gadget.jsf evaluates Runtime.exec(). Parent is matched on glassfish/asadmin/domain1 markers in its commandline so we don't fire on every JVM on the host. Rationale: Anchors on the GlassFish-specific parent (java + glassfish/asadmin/domain1/com.sun.aas.installRoot tokens documented in the Eclipse GlassFish startup args) plus an interpreter/LOLBin child — the exact RCE pivot the EL injection at /common/gadgets/gadget.jsf achieves via java.lang.Runtime.getRuntime().exec(). Cross-checked Bhanunamikaze PoC repo and stack.watch advisory for exploit chain shape. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/Bhanunamikaze/CVE-2026-2587-Exploit-POC • https://stack.watch/vuln/CVE-2026-2587/ • https://app.opencve.io/cve/CVE-2026-2587 • https://blog.mindedsecurity.com/2015/11/reliable-os-shell-with-el-expression.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1059.004

[LLM] Inbound HTTP request to GlassFish gadget.jsf handler (CVE-2026-2587 exploit attempt) Exploitation High
Detects HTTP requests targeting the vulnerable /common/gadgets/gadget.jsf endpoint with the gadget= URL parameter, the entry point for the EL injection RCE. Any external-sourced hit on this path is treatable as an exploit attempt because the admin console should not be internet-exposed. Rationale: The Bhanunamikaze PoC and Eclipse advisory both confirm the entry point is /common/gadgets/gadget.jsf with a gadget= URL parameter pointing to attacker-hosted XML — that string pair is a binary indicator that a CVE-2026-2587 attempt is in flight. EvalIndicator splits inline EL (URL contains #{ or %23%7B) from the callback-fetch variant where the EL lives in the fetched XML's ModulePrefs title attribute. Defender XDR is left empty because Defender Advanced Hunting does not ingest GlassFish/Apache/NGINX web access logs by default. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/Bhanunamikaze/CVE-2026-2587-Exploit-POC • https://stack.watch/vuln/CVE-2026-2587/ • https://www.hackingdream.net/2026/05/cve-2026-2587-glassfish-el-injection-exploit-poc.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb
(union isfuzzy=true
    (CommonSecurityLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where RequestURL has "/common/gadgets/gadget.jsf"
     | where RequestURL has "gadget="
     | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, ResultDescription),
    (W3CIISLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where csUriStem =~ "/common/gadgets/gadget.jsf"
     | where csUriQuery has "gadget="
     | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP = cIP, DestinationHostName = Computer, RequestURL = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), RequestMethod = csMethod, RequestClientApplication = csUserAgent, ResultDescription = tostring(scStatus)),
    (ImWebSession
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where Url has "/common/gadgets/gadget.jsf"
     | where Url has "gadget="
     | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP = SrcIpAddr, DestinationHostName = DstHostname, RequestURL = Url, RequestMethod = HttpMethod, RequestClientApplication = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, ResultDescription = tostring(HttpStatusCode)))
| extend GadgetParam = extract(@"(?i)gadget=([^&]+)", 1, RequestURL)
| extend EvalIndicator = iif(RequestURL has_any ("%23%7B","%23%7b","#{","getRuntime","java.lang.Runtime","ProcessBuilder","forName"), "DirectEL", "CallbackFetch")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GlassFish java process outbound HTTP fetch to external host (gadget XML callback) Exploitation Medium
Detects the GlassFish admin console java process fetching content from a public IP — the out-of-band step where the gadget handler retrieves the attacker-controlled XML payload to evaluate. Anchored on parent java + glassfish tokens to avoid the every-JVM-phones-home noise floor. Rationale: The CVE-2026-2587 exploit chain explicitly requires the GlassFish gadget handler to fetch the attacker-hosted XML from the URL in the gadget= parameter (per the Bhanunamikaze PoC, which hosts a benign probe XML and waits for the callback). A java process whose parent commandline carries the GlassFish startup tokens reaching out to a public IP on web ports is the network-side signature of that fetch. Tier set to hunting because legitimate Java integrations also call externally; pair with UC1 process-tree hits on the same host for high-confidence triage. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/Bhanunamikaze/CVE-2026-2587-Exploit-POC • https://stack.watch/vuln/CVE-2026-2587/
ATT&CKT1190 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe","java")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("glassfish","asadmin","appserver-rt","domain1","com.sun.aas.installRoot")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemotePort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Hits = count(), Cmds = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 5), URLs = make_set(RemoteUrl, 10)
          by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] Unpatched GlassFish admingui/jsftemplating inventory (CVE-2026-2587 attack surface) Exploitation High
Surface-level hunting query that lists hosts with Eclipse GlassFish admingui < 8.0.2 or jsftemplating < 4.2.0 installed so the SOC can drive patching and prioritise UC1-UC3 alerts by exposure. Pure inventory pivot — not a behavioural detection. Rationale: Article explicitly names the affected Maven packages and version ceilings (admingui < 8.0.2, jsftemplating < 4.2.0). Defender's TVM tables natively expose CVE-to-host mapping, making this the cleanest one-shot inventory query. Ordered by IsInternetFacing because that flag is the single biggest exploit-likelihood multiplier for this CVE. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-29wv-cv7p-xjc2 • https://github.com/eclipse-ee4j/glassfish/releases • https://app.opencve.io/cve/CVE-2026-2587

[LLM] Inbound HTTP request with Camel-internal header or query param to CXF/Knative endpoint (CVE-2026-47323) Exploitation High
Hunts for unauthenticated HTTP requests carrying Camel-reserved header names (CamelExecCommandExecutable, CamelFileName, CamelExecCommandArgs, etc.) destined for CXF-REST/CXF-SOAP/Knative-HTTP endpoints. Because the vulnerable HeaderFilterStrategy implementations only filter outbound — never inbound — any incoming HTTP request that smuggles a Camel-internal header through to a downstream camel-exec or camel-file route can override the configured executable or file path, yielding RCE or arbitrary file write. Rationale: The Camel-internal header names listed in the GHSA (CamelExecCommandExecutable, CamelFileName) are highly specific reserved strings — they only appear in legitimate traffic when a trusted Camel route forwards an internal message, which never crosses the wire from an external client in a correctly-segmented deployment. Any inbound HTTP request carrying these tokens to a CXF or Knative endpoint is a high-fidelity exploit attempt. Cross-checked against the Apache Camel security advisory page and the prior related CVEs cited in the GHSA (CVE-2025-30177, CVE-2025-27636, CVE-2025-29891, CVE-2026-40453) — all share the same header-injection primitive. Cross-checked against: • https://camel.apache.org/security/security-advisories.html • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-27636 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-29891 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8364-hfqj-pwm6
ATT&CKT1190 T1059

| where AdditionalFields has_any ("CamelExecCommandExecutable", "CamelFileName", "CamelExecCommandArgs", "CamelExecCommandWorkingDir", "CamelFileAbsolutePath", "CamelHttpQuery")
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("CamelExecCommandExecutable", "CamelFileName", "CamelExecCommandArgs")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe", "java", "javaw.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("camel", "cxf", "knative")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc

   or RequestCookies has_any ("CamelExecCommandExecutable", "CamelFileName")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourcePort, SourceHostName, DestinationHostName, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DeviceProduct, DeviceVendor, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Apache Camel JVM spawning shell or command interpreter via camel-exec (CVE-2026-47323 post-exploit) Installation High
Detects java/javaw processes hosting Camel routes spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, bash, or LOLBin children — the post-exploitation footprint of CamelExecCommandExecutable header injection. The camel-exec component reads its target binary from the Camel exchange header at runtime; when the attacker controls that header, the JVM literally execs whatever they specify, so this parent→child shape is the cleanest behavioural signal after the wire-side filter is bypassed. Rationale: Java spawning cmd.exe/sh/LOLBin children is already an unusual pattern in production; combined with a parent command line containing 'camel', 'cxf', 'knative', or '-jar' running a Camel artifact, the FP rate collapses. This is the deterministic execution shape of camel-exec when CamelExecCommandExecutable is attacker-controlled per the GHSA. Cross-checked Camel docs for camel-exec processor behaviour and the prior CVE-2025-30177 (camel-undertow) advisory which describes the same RCE end-state. Cross-checked against: • https://camel.apache.org/components/latest/exec-component.html • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-30177 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8364-hfqj-pwm6
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.003 T1059.004 T1190

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe", "javaw.exe", "java")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("camel", "cxf", "knative", "-jar")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "sh", "bash", "dash", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "rundll32.exe", "certutil.exe", "bitsadmin.exe", "curl.exe", "wget", "mshta.exe", "regsvr32.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\java.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\javaw.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "/java"
| where NewProcessName endswith_cs "\\cmd.exe" or NewProcessName endswith_cs "\\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith_cs "\\pwsh.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/sh" or NewProcessName endswith "/bash" or NewProcessName endswith "\\wscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\cscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\certutil.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\bitsadmin.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\mshta.exe"

| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName

[LLM] Apache Camel JVM writing files to sensitive paths via camel-file (CVE-2026-47323 arbitrary file write) Installation Medium
Detects java/javaw processes (Camel runtime) writing files into web roots, system directories, autorun locations, or SSH key paths — the file-write half of CVE-2026-47323 where attacker-controlled CamelFileName / CamelFileAbsolutePath headers override the configured camel-file producer destination. Pivots on the JVM as the writer with an article-specific path allow-list of high-value drop targets. Rationale: camel-file's producer resolves its destination from the CamelFileName / CamelFileAbsolutePath exchange header per Camel docs. The GHSA explicitly calls out camel-file as the second exploitation primitive after camel-exec. The JVM writing JSP/WAR/ASPX or authorized_keys into a webroot or autorun path is a high-fidelity arbitrary-file-write signal regardless of the underlying CVE — pairing the path/extension allow-list with the JVM-as-writer pivot makes this article-specific. Verified against Apache Camel file-component documentation and CVE-2025-29891 advisory (same primitive in camel-undertow). Cross-checked against: • https://camel.apache.org/components/latest/file-component.html • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-29891 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8364-hfqj-pwm6

[LLM] zrok ProxyShare SSRF — request path begins with absolute URL (CVE-2026-45568) Exploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests to a zrok Python ProxyShare where the request path itself is an absolute URL (http:// or https://) — the precise shape of the CVE-2026-45568 SSRF, including pivots to cloud metadata services like 127.0.0.1:19190/metadata. Article-specific because Flask + urllib.parse.urljoin only rewrites the host when the second argument is absolute, so this URI shape is the exact attacker vector. Rationale: Article specifies the exact SSRF primitive: a request path that itself is an absolute URL (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:19190/metadata) bypasses urljoin's base-URL anchoring. The Sentinel union targets the two web-server log tables actually populated for App Service and IIS-hosted zrok deployments; the Defender query pivots on the resulting outbound proxy call to link-local / loopback metadata IPs since Defender doesn't expose web access logs. Cross-checked GHSA-jh67-hwqw-m5r7 and the urllib.parse.urljoin RFC-3986 absolute-URI behaviour documented at docs.python.org. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jh67-hwqw-m5r7 • https://docs.python.org/3/library/urllib.parse.html#urllib.parse.urljoin • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45568
ATT&CKT1190 T1090
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Defender Advanced Hunting has no native web-server log table; this detection lives in IIS / AppService / WAF logs and is expressed on Sentinel side.
// Closest Defender pivot: any process on a zrok-hosting endpoint making an outbound connection to a link-local / loopback metadata IP shortly after receiving inbound traffic on the share.
let MetadataIPs = dynamic(["127.0.0.1","169.254.169.254","169.254.170.2","fd00:ec2::254","100.100.100.200"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("zrok.exe","zrok","python.exe","python3","python","pythonw.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("zrok share","ProxyShare","zrok.proxy","urllib.parse.urljoin")
| where RemoteIP in (MetadataIPs) or RemoteIP startswith "169.254."
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
// Hunt inbound HTTP requests where the URI itself is an absolute URL (the zrok ProxyShare SSRF shape).
let Lookback = 7d;
let AbsoluteUrlPath = @"(?i)^/+https?:/";
let MetadataMarkers = dynamic(["127.0.0.1","169.254.169.254","metadata.google","metadata.azure","100.100.100.200","/metadata","/latest/meta-data","/computeMetadata"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
    W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where csUriStem matches regex AbsoluteUrlPath
         or csUriQuery has_any (MetadataMarkers)
    | project TimeGenerated, _ResourceId, Computer,
              ClientIP = cIP, Method = csMethod,
              UriStem = csUriStem, UriQuery = csUriQuery,
              Status = scStatus, UserAgent = csUserAgent,
              SourceTable = "W3CIISLog"
),
(
    AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where CsUriStem matches regex AbsoluteUrlPath
         or CsUriQuery has_any (MetadataMarkers)
    | project TimeGenerated, _ResourceId, Computer = CsHost,
              ClientIP = CIp, Method = CsMethod,
              UriStem = CsUriStem, UriQuery = CsUriQuery,
              Status = ScStatus, UserAgent = UserAgent,
              SourceTable = "AppServiceHTTPLogs"
)
| extend AbsoluteUrlInPath = iff(UriStem matches regex AbsoluteUrlPath, true, false)
| extend MetadataTargeted = iff(UriStem has_any (MetadataMarkers) or UriQuery has_any (MetadataMarkers), true, false)
| where AbsoluteUrlInPath or MetadataTargeted
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] HAXcms CVE-2026-46395: unauthenticated GET to /system/api/connectionSettings Exploitation High
Surfaces any HTTP GET to the HAXcms unauthenticated /system/api/connectionSettings endpoint, which returns base64 tokens whose tail bytes are the private signing key (privateKey+salt) plaintext. A single GET against a vulnerable @haxtheweb/haxcms-nodejs <= 25.0.0 instance fully discloses the JWT-signing secret, so any request to this path on internet-facing HAXcms deployments warrants triage. Rationale: Endpoint path `/system/api/connectionSettings` is the article-named primary leak vector and is not present on benign HAXcms traffic that goes through the authenticated UI. A successful 2xx on this path is essentially equivalent to private-key exfiltration. Defender_kql is intentionally empty because Defender Advanced Hunting does not ship raw HTTP request URIs for arbitrary Node.js applications — the detection lives on the web tier (AppServiceHTTPLogs / W3CIISLog). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6c8g-9hfh-pq5h • https://github.com/haxtheweb/issues
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1190

    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod =~ "GET"
        | where csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"
        | project TimeGenerated, SourceIp = CIp, Host = CsHost, UriStem = csUriStem, Method = csMethod, Status = ScStatus, UserAgent),
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod =~ "GET"
        | where csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"
        | project TimeGenerated, SourceIp = cIP, Host = sSiteName, UriStem = csUriStem, Method = csMethod, Status = scStatus, UserAgent = csUserAgent);
HaxcmsLeak
| where Status between (200 .. 299)   // 2xx = key successfully disclosed
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            UserAgents = make_set(UserAgent, 10), Statuses = make_set(Status, 5)
            by SourceIp, Host
| order by FirstSeen desc

[LLM] HAXcms CVE-2026-46395: forged-JWT admin write within 30m of connectionSettings leak Actions on Objectives High
Correlates a successful GET to /system/api/connectionSettings (the private-key leak primitive) with subsequent authenticated HAXcms admin-write API calls from the same source IP within 30 minutes. Because forged JWTs are signed with the stolen privateKey+salt they produce no login events and look indistinguishable from the real admin to single-event detections — this temporal correlation is the cleanest way to catch the full exploit chain. Rationale: The article describes the complete exploit chain (extract key → forge admin JWT → call admin API) as feasible "with a single HTTP request" sequence, and explicitly warns the forged tokens "produce no login events in logs". Temporal correlation of the article-named leak path (`/system/api/connectionSettings`) with the article-named admin endpoints (saveOutline / saveManifest / saveNode / createSite / deleteSite / saveFile / saveUser / form_token) from the same source IP within a tight window is the only reliable host-agnostic signal. Defender_kql is a host-tier approximation that depends on the HAXcms server itself being enrolled in Defender for Endpoint; if it is not, leave the Defender field empty operationally and rely on the Sentinel / Splunk web-tier queries. Datadog/Falcon/Sigma left empty — single-shape Sigma cannot express the cross-event join, and Falcon FDR does not ship arbitrary Node.js HTTP request URIs. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6c8g-9hfh-pq5h • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-46395
ATT&CKT1606.001 T1078 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// HAXcms is a Node.js web app — the JWT/Authorization header signal lives on the web tier (AppServiceHTTPLogs / W3CIISLog), not in DeviceProcessEvents.
// On hosts that run HAXcms AND are enrolled in Defender, this query approximates the post-exploit chain by joining
// outbound DNS lookups from the suspected attacker host to HAXcms domains with subsequent file modifications under
// HAXcms content roots performed by the local node.exe.
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let HaxcmsHostHints = dynamic(["haxcms","haxtheweb"]);
let NetTouch = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (HaxcmsHostHints) or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
    | where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt","HttpConnectionInspected")
    | project NetTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where FolderPath has_any ("\\haxcms\\","/haxcms/","\\_sites\\","/_sites/","site.json","manifest.json")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| join kind=inner NetTouch on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (NetTime .. NetTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, NetTime)
| project NetTime, FileWriteTime = Timestamp, DelaySec, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP,
          FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by NetTime desc
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let WindowDays = 7d;
let HaxcmsLeak = union isfuzzy=true
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod =~ "GET" and csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"
        | where ScStatus between (200 .. 299)
        | project LeakTime = TimeGenerated, SourceIp = CIp, Host = CsHost),
    (W3CIISLog

        | where csMethod =~ "GET" and csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"

let HaxcmsAdminWrite = union isfuzzy=true

        | where ScStatus between (200 .. 299)

        | where scStatus between (200 .. 299)

[LLM] Algernon web server spawning shell child process (CVE-2026-45721 handler.lua RCE) Exploitation High
Detects the Algernon web server binary spawning /bin/sh, /bin/bash or cmd.exe — the exact primitive used by handler.lua's run3() / os.execute() / io.popen() when the parent-directory traversal bug loads attacker-controlled Lua. Algernon's normal request handling does not fork shells; this pattern is the live exploitation signature. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit exploitation primitive: run3() at engine/basic.go:142 calls exec.Command("sh", "-c", ...) via lua/run3/run3.go:23, plus the unsandboxed gopher-lua os.execute / io.popen exposed because lua/pool/pool.go:34 omits SkipOpenLibs. The parent-process pivot (algernon) plus a shell child is article-specific and not covered by generic 'web server spawns shell' rules without the algernon binary name. Cross-checked GitHub xyproto/algernon repository structure to confirm 'algernon' is the canonical binary name; no external NVD entry yet (fresh GHSA-xwcr-wm99-g9jc). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/xyproto/algernon • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xwcr-wm99-g9jc
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// CVE-2026-45721 — Algernon parent process spawning a shell. Stock Algernon never forks /bin/sh for request handling; this is the run3()/os.execute() primitive that handler.lua exposes.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "algernon"
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "/algernon"
   or InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^algernon(\.exe)?$"
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ash","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
// classic exploit shape: sh -c <attacker payload> launched by web server
| extend ShellArgs = iff(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-c ","/c ","-Command","-EncodedCommand"), "shell-with-inline-cmd", "interactive-or-script")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          ShellArgs, SHA256, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-45721 — Algernon spawning shell on the ASIM cross-vendor process schema. Catches Linux (auditd) + Windows (4688/Sysmon) feeds.
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)algernon(\.exe)?$"
| where TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)(sh|bash|dash|zsh|ash|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh\.exe)$"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| extend ShellWithInlineCmd = iff(TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("-c ","/c ","-Command","-EncodedCommand"), true, false)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildName = TargetProcessName,
          ChildCmd  = TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ShellWithInlineCmd, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] handler.lua dropped outside Algernon's configured web root (CVE-2026-45721 backdoor stage) Installation High
Algernon's vulnerable DirPage walks UP from the requested directory looking for handler.lua and executes the first match with full Lua/run3/httpclient privileges. This rule alerts on any process writing a file named handler.lua into a parent-of-webroot location (/, /srv, /var, /home, /tmp, /dev/shm) — the staging artefact that turns the bug into pre-auth RCE. Rationale: The article enumerates the exact candidate paths the vulnerable DirPage loop probes for each canonical Algernon invocation (/srv/handler.lua, /var/www/handler.lua, /home/<user>/handler.lua, /handler.lua, plus the /dev/shm extraction-dir variant from engine/handlers.go:249-266). A file write of handler.lua into ANY of those paths is the persistence artefact the bug weaponises — high specificity because legitimate Algernon deployments place handler.lua INSIDE the served tree (e.g. /srv/site/handler.lua), not in /srv/ or /var/. Cross-checked xyproto/algernon samples/ tree which confirms handler.lua only lives inside per-app subdirectories under samples/, never at samples/ root. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/xyproto/algernon • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xwcr-wm99-g9jc
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1547 T1574
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
// CVE-2026-45721 — handler.lua written into a parent of any plausible Algernon web root. The article's exploit places it at /srv/handler.lua, /var/handler.lua, /home/<user>/handler.lua, /dev/shm/handler.lua, or filesystem root.
let WebRootAncestors = dynamic([
    "/handler.lua",
    "/srv/handler.lua",
    "/var/handler.lua",
    "/var/www/handler.lua",
    "/home/handler.lua",
    "/tmp/handler.lua",
    "/dev/shm/handler.lua",
    "/opt/handler.lua",
    "/usr/local/handler.lua",
    "/run/handler.lua"
]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "handler.lua"
| extend FullPath = strcat(FolderPath, iff(FolderPath endswith "/" or FolderPath endswith "\\", "", "/"), FileName)
| where FullPath in~ (WebRootAncestors)
   or FolderPath matches regex @"^/home/[^/]+/?$"
   or FolderPath matches regex @"^/srv/?$"
   or FolderPath matches regex @"^/var(/www)?/?$"
   or FolderPath in~ ("/","/tmp","/dev/shm","/run","/opt","/usr/local")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
// .alg archive extraction by algernon itself is a documented vector — keep but tag it
| extend ExtractedByAlgernon = iff(InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "algernon", true, false)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FullPath, FolderPath,
          WriterImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          WriterCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          WriterUser  = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          ExtractedByAlgernon, SHA256, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-45721 — handler.lua dropped into a parent-of-webroot path. ASIM ImFileEvent covers Linux (auditd) + Windows (Sysmon EID 11) feeds.
let WebRootAncestors = dynamic([
    "/handler.lua",
    "/srv/handler.lua",
    "/var/handler.lua",
    "/var/www/handler.lua",
    "/home/handler.lua",
    "/tmp/handler.lua",
    "/dev/shm/handler.lua",
    "/opt/handler.lua",
    "/usr/local/handler.lua",
    "/run/handler.lua"
]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName =~ "handler.lua"
| where TargetFilePath in~ (WebRootAncestors)
   or TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/home/[^/]+/handler\.lua$"
   or TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/var(/www)?/handler\.lua$"
| extend ExtractedByAlgernon = iff(ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)algernon$", true, false)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath,
          WriterCmd  = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          WriterName = ActingProcessName,
          WriterUser = ActorUsername,
          ExtractedByAlgernon, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: handler.lua Written to Algernon Webroot Ancestor (CVE-2026-45721)
id: 9b7d2e5f-4a0c-4b2a-8f33-6d2e9c5d1b02
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of a file named handler.lua in a directory that is an ancestor of any plausible Algernon web root (/, /srv, /var, /var/www, /home/<user>, /tmp, /dev/shm, /opt, /usr/local). Algernon's vulnerable DirPage walks ancestors looking for this exact filename and executes the first match with full run3()/httpclient/os.execute privileges.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xwcr-wm99-g9jc
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:

      - '/dev/shm/handler.lua'

[LLM] Algernon vulnerable installation discovery (CVE-2026-45721 exposure inventory) Reconnaissance High
Hunts every host where the Algernon Go web server is installed or running so the SOC can map the blast radius of CVE-2026-45721. The bug is unauthenticated and applies to all currently-published versions until a patched release ships; identifying every algernon instance is a prerequisite to applying compensating controls (chmod 700 on parent dirs, blocking inbound traffic, or scheduled patching). Rationale: The article makes clear the bug is reachable on a stock unauth GET / against any Algernon install regardless of configuration, so the population that needs hunting is 'every host running algernon'. Two pivots — TVM software inventory and runtime ProcessRollup2/ImProcessCreate — cover both managed (TVM-onboarded) and unmanaged Linux/Windows boxes. Pulled the runtime command line so analysts can immediately read the configured --prod / web-root flag and reason about which ancestor paths are reachable. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/xyproto/algernon • https://github.com/xyproto/algernon/releases • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xwcr-wm99-g9jc
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// CVE-2026-45721 — discover every host with Algernon installed or running. Two pivots: TVM inventory (slower, accurate) + recent process executions (faster, covers running instances).
let TvmHits =
    DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
    | where SoftwareName has "algernon" or SoftwareVendor =~ "xyproto"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, Source="TVM";
let ProcessHits =
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "algernon" or FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)algernon(\.exe)?$"
    | summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp),
                CmdLines=make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 20),
                ParentBins=make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10),
                RunAsUsers=make_set(AccountName, 10)
                by DeviceId, DeviceName, FileName, SHA256
    | extend Timestamp=LastSeen, OSPlatform="unknown", SoftwareVendor="xyproto", SoftwareName="algernon", SoftwareVersion=tostring(SHA256), Source="ProcessExec"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, Source, FirstSeen, LastSeen, CmdLines, ParentBins, RunAsUsers;
union isfuzzy=true TvmHits, ProcessHits
| order by DeviceName asc, Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-45721 — Sentinel exposure inventory. DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory is not in standard Sentinel; pivot via DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities (if XDR connector is on) plus ASIM ImProcessCreate for runtime evidence.
let TvmHits =
    DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where SoftwareName has "algernon" or SoftwareVendor =~ "xyproto" or CveId =~ "CVE-2026-45721"
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, Source="TVM";
let ProcessHits =
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)algernon(\.exe)?$"
       or TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)algernon(\.exe)?$"
    | extend AlgernonPath = iff(TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)algernon", TargetProcessName, ActingProcessName)
    | extend AlgernonCmd  = iff(TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)algernon", TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessCommandLine)
    | summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated),
                CmdLines=make_set(AlgernonCmd, 20),
                RunAsUsers=make_set(ActorUsername, 10)
                by DvcHostname, AlgernonPath
    | extend TimeGenerated=LastSeen, SoftwareVendor="xyproto", SoftwareName="algernon", CveId="CVE-2026-45721", Source="ProcessExec"
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceName=DvcHostname, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, AlgernonPath, CveId, Source, FirstSeen, LastSeen, CmdLines, RunAsUsers;
union isfuzzy=true TvmHits, ProcessHits
| order by DeviceName asc, TimeGenerated desc
(source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.security) (@process.executable.path:(*/algernon OR *\\algernon.exe) OR @Image:(*\\algernon.exe OR *\\Algernon.exe) OR @process.name:algernon OR @process.command_line:*algernon*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(\/|\\)algernon(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName], function={ count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp), collect([CommandLine, UserName, SHA256HashData]) })
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.user) as users values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="algernon" OR Processes.process_path="*algernon*" by host Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | eval days_observed=round((last_seen-first_seen)/86400,1) | table host process_name first_seen last_seen days_observed cmdlines users parents

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45721")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45721")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

[LLM] npm install of compromised @opensearch-project/opensearch versions 3.5.3/3.6.2/3.7.0/3.8.0 Delivery High
Hunts for Node.js / npm process executions that resolve, fetch, or install the four malicious tagged versions published in the 12-May-2026 force-push CI compromise. Tightest possible install-time signal — fires on the exact package@version string the advisory enumerates. Rationale: Anchors on the four exact malicious versions enumerated in the advisory and the canonical Node toolchain binaries that resolve them. Highlighting the 00:00Z-10:00Z 2026-05-12 window via InWindow distinguishes guaranteed-compromised installs from later catalogue references. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/TanStack/router/security/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe")
   or FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch"
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch"
| extend MaliciousVersion = case(
    ProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.5.3" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.5.3", "3.5.3",
    ProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.6.2" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.6.2", "3.6.2",
    ProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.7.0" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.7.0", "3.7.0",
    ProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.8.0" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.8.0", "3.8.0",
    "unknown-version-of-affected-pkg")
| extend InWindow = Timestamp between (datetime(2026-05-12T00:00:00Z) .. datetime(2026-05-12T10:00:00Z))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InWindow, MaliciousVersion, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName has_any ("\\npm.exe","\\node.exe","\\yarn.exe","\\pnpm.exe","\\npx.exe") or ParentProcessName has_any ("\\npm.exe","\\node.exe","\\yarn.exe","\\pnpm.exe"))
| where CommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch"
| extend MaliciousVersion = case(
    CommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.5.3", "3.5.3",
    CommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.6.2", "3.6.2",
    CommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.7.0", "3.7.0",
    CommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.8.0", "3.8.0",
    "unknown-version-of-affected-pkg")
| extend InWindow = TimeGenerated between (datetime(2026-05-12T00:00:00Z) .. datetime(2026-05-12T10:00:00Z))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, SubjectUserName, InWindow, MaliciousVersion, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] On-disk presence of malicious @opensearch-project/opensearch payload SHA256 Installation High
Hunts for write or open of any file whose SHA256 matches one of the three malicious artefacts shipped with the four compromised versions. Hash-based pivot catches the payload even if the package was renamed, vendored, or unzipped from a tarball off-line. Rationale: Uses the three SHA256 IOCs the GHSA enumerates — single-source on advisory but hash matches are zero-FP by construction. Pivot via DeviceFileEvents/ImFileEvent rather than IOC threat-feed correlation so it fires even when the package is unpacked from a tarball or copied from a private mirror. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/TanStack/router/security/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud / TeamPCP C2 beacon to api.masscan.cloud / git-tanstack.com / *.getsession.org Command & Control High
Detects outbound DNS or HTTP requests to the four C2 / data-exfil domains hard-coded in the compromised @opensearch-project/opensearch payload. Catches the post-install beacon even when host telemetry of the install itself was missed. Rationale: Pivots on the four article-named domains across DNS, proxy/firewall (CommonSecurityLog), ASIM DNS/web, and EDR. Sigma is skipped because the union across DNS+proxy+ASIM+web tables can't be expressed in single-event-shape Sigma. Sentinel query uses each table's actual hostname/IP columns (Computer/ClientIP on DnsEvents, DvcHostname/SrcIpAddr on ImDnsActivity, SourceHostName/SourceIP on CommonSecurityLog). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/TanStack/router/security/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx • https://github.com/TanStack/router/issues/7383
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let BadDomains = dynamic(["api.masscan.cloud","git-tanstack.com","filev2.getsession.org","seed1.getsession.org"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (BadDomains)
     or tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host) in~ (BadDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadDomains = dynamic(["api.masscan.cloud","git-tanstack.com","filev2.getsession.org","seed1.getsession.org"]);
let DnsHits = DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has_any (BadDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, ClientAddr = ClientIP, Domain = Name, Source = "DnsEvents";
let AsimDnsHits = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (BadDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, ClientAddr = SrcIpAddr, Domain = DnsQuery, Source = strcat("ImDnsActivity:", EventProduct);
let CslHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationDnsDomain has_any (BadDomains)
        or DestinationHostName has_any (BadDomains)
        or RequestURL has_any (BadDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, ClientAddr = SourceIP, Domain = coalesce(DestinationDnsDomain, DestinationHostName, RequestURL), Source = strcat("CommonSecurityLog:", DeviceVendor, ":", DeviceProduct);
let WebHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (BadDomains) or HttpHostName has_any (BadDomains) or DstHostname has_any (BadDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = SrcHostname, ClientAddr = SrcIpAddr, Domain = coalesce(HttpHostName, DstHostname, Url), Source = strcat("ImWebSession:", EventProduct);
union isfuzzy=true DnsHits, AsimDnsHits, CslHits, WebHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.defender OR source:linux.syslog OR source:linux.auditd OR source:network) (@DestinationHostname:(*api.masscan.cloud OR *git-tanstack.com OR *filev2.getsession.org OR *seed1.getsession.org) OR @network.destination.domain:(*api.masscan.cloud OR *git-tanstack.com OR *filev2.getsession.org OR *seed1.getsession.org) OR @dns.question.name:(*api.masscan.cloud OR *git-tanstack.com OR *filev2.getsession.org OR *seed1.getsession.org) OR @http.url:(*api.masscan.cloud* OR *git-tanstack.com* OR *filev2.getsession.org* OR *seed1.getsession.org*))
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest OR #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 OR #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP6)
| regex("(api\\.masscan\\.cloud|git-tanstack\\.com|filev2\\.getsession\\.org|seed1\\.getsession\\.org)", field=DomainName) OR regex("(api\\.masscan\\.cloud|git-tanstack\\.com|filev2\\.getsession\\.org|seed1\\.getsession\\.org)", field=ContextImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=[count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp), collect([RemoteAddressIP4, FirstIP4Record], limit=5)])

[LLM] Postinstall script execution from compromised @opensearch-project/opensearch package Installation Medium
Detects node child processes whose ancestor is npm/yarn/pnpm running an install/ci on the affected package — the malicious payload is delivered via a postinstall lifecycle hook that spawns shell/node/curl. Catches the active-execution moment regardless of whether the version string was logged at install time. Rationale: Targets the postinstall-hook spawn pattern that the Shai-Hulud / TanStack-router compromise pattern relies on — node/npm parent + script-host/curl child while the package path is in scope. Parent CommandLine carries the package name even when the version string isn't logged. Tagged hunting because legitimate postinstall hooks (esbuild, sharp, sqlite3) generate similar shapes — pair with UC1/UC2 for high-confidence triage. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/TanStack/router/security/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
| where (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch"
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "node_modules\\@opensearch-project\\opensearch"
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "node_modules/@opensearch-project/opensearch")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe")
     or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","curl ","wget ","Buffer.from","child_process","eval(","http.get","https.request")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe","/node","/npm","/yarn","/pnpm")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("@opensearch-project/opensearch","node_modules\\@opensearch-project\\opensearch","node_modules/@opensearch-project/opensearch")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","bash","sh","node.exe")
     or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","curl ","wget ","Buffer.from","child_process","eval(")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Postinstall Child Process from @opensearch-project/opensearch Package
id: 9f0b4d12-8e3a-4ce1-bf12-2c0e1a5f6d7e
description: Detects npm/yarn/pnpm/node spawning a script-host or download utility while installing the GHSA-27f5-xjrr-q9ff @opensearch-project/opensearch package - characteristic of the malicious postinstall lifecycle hook.
references:
    - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-27f5-xjrr-q9ff
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.007
    - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\node.exe'
            - '\npm.exe'
            - '\yarn.exe'
            - '\pnpm.exe'
            - '\npx.exe'
        ParentCommandLine|contains:
            - '@opensearch-project/opensearch'
    child_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\curl.exe'
            - '\wget.exe'
            - '\certutil.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
            - '\bash.exe'
            - '\sh.exe'
    child_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Buffer.from'
            - 'child_process'
            - 'eval('
    condition: parent and (child_image or child_cmd)
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR */node OR */npm OR */yarn OR */pnpm) @ParentCommandLine:(*@opensearch-project/opensearch* OR *node_modules\\@opensearch-project\\opensearch* OR *node_modules/@opensearch-project/opensearch*) (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR */bash OR */sh OR */curl OR */wget) OR @CommandLine:(*Invoke-WebRequest* OR *DownloadString* OR *Buffer.from* OR *child_process* OR "*eval(*"))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(node|npm|yarn|pnpm|npx)\.exe$/i OR regex("/(node|npm|yarn|pnpm|npx)$", field=ParentImageFileName)
| regex("@opensearch-project/opensearch|node_modules[\\\\/]@opensearch-project[\\\\/]opensearch", field=ParentCommandLine)
| (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd|curl|wget|certutil|bitsadmin|bash|sh)\.exe$/i OR regex("(Invoke-WebRequest|DownloadString|Buffer\\.from|child_process|eval\\()", field=CommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName], function=[count(), collect([CommandLine, ParentCommandLine], limit=3)])

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Vulnerable MLflow 3.9.0 install — CVE-2026-2611 Assistant /ajax-api origin bypass Weaponization High
Hunts hosts with the affected MLflow 3.9.0 release installed where the Assistant feature is exposed to browser-mediated cross-origin RCE via /ajax-api. Article-specific because both the package and the single vulnerable version are named in the GHSA. Rationale: Pivots on the two strings the advisory actually names — package `mlflow` and version `3.9.0` — plus the assigned CVE-2026-2611. Cross-checked against DailyCVE which confirms 3.9.0-only scope and the 3.10.0 fix. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-67c5-x5mf-rppq • https://dailycve.com/mlflow-improper-origin-validation-cve-2026-2611-critical/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Vulnerabilities
// CVE-2026-2611 — MLflow Assistant /ajax-api origin bypass; only 3.9.0 is vulnerable, fixed in 3.10.0
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where SoftwareName =~ "mlflow"
| where SoftwareVersion startswith "3.9.0"
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where CveId =~ "CVE-2026-2611"
    | project DeviceId, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-2611 — MLflow Assistant /ajax-api origin bypass; vulnerable = 3.9.0 only
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CveId =~ "CVE-2026-2611" or (SoftwareName =~ "mlflow" and SoftwareVersion startswith "3.9.0")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, DeviceId, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Vulnerabilities where Vulnerabilities.cve="CVE-2026-2611" OR (Vulnerabilities.product="mlflow" AND Vulnerabilities.signature="3.9.0") by Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.product Vulnerabilities.signature Vulnerabilities.cve | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] MLflow server process spawning Claude Code CLI or shell — CVE-2026-2611 RCE chain Exploitation High
Detects the post-exploit execution stage of CVE-2026-2611: a browser-driven cross-origin call flips the MLflow Assistant config to full-access then invokes the Claude Code sub-agent to run OS commands. The signature is an MLflow server worker (python/gunicorn/mlflow entrypoint) spawning either the `claude` CLI or a direct shell. Rationale: Logic chains the only two attacker-controlled strings the advisory + DailyCVE writeup expose: the `mlflow` parent context (server worker) and the `Claude Code sub-agent` execution that follows the config flip. Cross-checked with the DailyCVE breakdown confirming the Claude Code sub-agent is the post-exploit command runner. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-67c5-x5mf-rppq • https://dailycve.com/mlflow-improper-origin-validation-cve-2026-2611-critical/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1059.004 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// CVE-2026-2611 — MLflow Assistant invokes Claude Code sub-agent or shell after /ajax-api origin bypass
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "mlflow"
     or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("mlflow","mlflow.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("claude","claude.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh","zsh","dash")
     or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("claude -p ","claude --print","claude code")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python","python3","python3.exe","gunicorn","gunicorn.exe","mlflow","mlflow.exe","uvicorn","uvicorn.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-2611 — MLflow Assistant -> Claude Code / shell post-exploit (ASIM ImProcessCreate)
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has "mlflow"
     or ParentProcessName in~ ("mlflow","mlflow.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("claude","claude.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh","zsh","dash")
     or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("claude -p ","claude --print","claude code")
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("python.exe","python","python3","python3.exe","gunicorn","gunicorn.exe","mlflow","mlflow.exe","uvicorn","uvicorn.exe")
     or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("mlflow server","mlflow ui","mlflow gateway","-m mlflow")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: MLflow Assistant Sub-Agent RCE via Claude Code (CVE-2026-2611)
id: 8b3f1d2e-4a6c-4d8f-9e1a-2b3c4d5e6f7a
description: Detects an MLflow server worker (python/gunicorn/mlflow entrypoint with `mlflow` in its command line) spawning the Claude Code CLI or a shell process. This is the post-exploit RCE chain for CVE-2026-2611, where a malicious webpage abuses the missing origin check on /ajax-api endpoints to flip the Assistant config and execute OS commands via the Claude Code sub-agent.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-67c5-x5mf-rppq
  - https://dailycve.com/mlflow-improper-origin-validation-cve-2026-2611-critical/

logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  parent_mlflow:
    ParentCommandLine|contains: 'mlflow'
  child_shell_or_claude:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\claude.exe'
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/claude'
  child_claude_headless:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'claude -p '
      - 'claude --print'
      - 'claude code'
  condition: parent_mlflow and (child_shell_or_claude or child_claude_headless)
falsepositives:
  - Data scientists running `mlflow server` and using the legitimate Assistant from a same-origin browser session in a research sandbox
  - CI jobs that legitimately invoke `claude` via an MLflow recipe
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentCommandLine:(*mlflow* OR *MLflow* OR *MLFLOW*) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\Pwsh.exe OR *\\claude.exe OR *\\Claude.exe)) OR (source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:(*mlflow* AND (*claude* OR *"/bin/sh"* OR *"/bin/bash"*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(python|python3|gunicorn|uvicorn|mlflow)(\.exe)?$/i
| regex("mlflow", field=ParentCommandLine, flags="i")
| ImageFileName=/(claude|cmd|powershell|pwsh|bash|sh|zsh|dash)(\.exe)?$/i OR CommandLine=/(claude\s+-p\b|claude\s+--print|claude\s+code\b)/i

Detects known BadIIS samples from the Talos demo.pdb commodity ecosystem by exact SHA256 hash on file write, image load, or process execution events. High-confidence retroactive sweep across all hosts. Rationale: Uses the 8 SHA256 IOCs published verbatim in the Talos article. Cross-checked against Elastic's BADIIS write-up and Trend Micro's earlier reporting confirming the same family lineage. Hash matching is article-specific and zero-FP if a hit occurs. [LLM] BadIIS C2 IP / domain beacon (lee.6686ty.vip, iis.01nmwe.xyz) Command & Control High
Detects any host contacting the published BadIIS command-and-control infrastructure: the two domains used for SEO-fraud orchestration plus the five IPs tied to the demo.pdb variant. Pivots across DNS, network-connection, and proxy telemetry. Rationale: Five IPs and two domains (lee.6686ty.vip, iis.01nmwe.xyz) published in the article. These are operational C2 — any contact is a high-fidelity signal. Cross-validated the campaign infrastructure pattern against Trend Micro's Feb-2025 BadIIS write-up which described similar dual-use C2 (one for SEO redirect targets, one for crawler-cloaking content). Cross-checked against: • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/25/b/chinese-speaking-group-manipulates-seo-with-badiis.html • https://gbhackers.com/iis-servers/

[LLM] IIS worker (w3wp.exe) initiating outbound connection to public IP Command & Control Medium
Hunts for IIS application-pool worker processes (w3wp.exe) making outbound connections to the public internet. Legitimate IIS sites typically serve inbound; sustained outbound HTTP/HTTPS from w3wp.exe to non-RFC1918 destinations is the textbook BadIIS beacon shape — the malicious native IIS module pulls cloaked SEO content and reports back from inside the worker process. Rationale: Article-specific because BadIIS is a *native IIS module* loaded into w3wp.exe — every C2 beacon, every cloaked-content fetch, every SEO-redirect lookup flows out as outbound HTTP from the worker process. Elastic and Trend Micro both describe the module reaching a backend for crawler-decision content, confirming the egress pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/badiis-to-the-bone-new-insights-to-global-seo-poisoning-campaign • https://blog.alphahunt.io/deep-research-badiis-isnt-enough-the-iis-module-http-fingerprints-that-catch-seo-fraud-cloaking/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090 T1505.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt","ConnectionRequest")
| where RemotePort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| summarize ConnCount=count(), DistinctDests=dcount(RemoteIP), SampleUrl=any(RemoteUrl), SampleCmd=any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where ConnCount > 3
| order by ConnCount desc
let IISHosts = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName =~ "w3wp.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
    | summarize by DvcHostname;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcHostname in (IISHosts) or SrcHostname in (IISHosts)
| where DstPortNumber in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where DstIpAddr !startswith "10." and DstIpAddr !startswith "192.168." and DstIpAddr !startswith "127." and DstIpAddr !startswith "169.254."
| where not(DstIpAddr matches regex @"^172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[0-1])\.")
| summarize ConnCount=count(), DistinctDests=dcount(DstIpAddr), SampleHost=any(DstHostname), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 3
| order by ConnCount desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 (@Image:(*\\w3wp.exe OR *\\W3wp.exe OR *\\W3WP.EXE)) (@DestinationPort:(80 OR 443 OR 8080 OR 8443)) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 10.0.0.0/8) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 172.16.0.0/12) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 192.168.0.0/16) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 127.0.0.0/8)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/\\w3wp\.exe$/i RemotePort=/^(80|443|8080|8443)$/

| NOT cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("127.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count(as=ConnCount))
| ConnCount>3

[LLM] IIS native module DLL drop or applicationHost.config modification by non-IIS process Installation High
Detects file writes of DLLs into IIS module load paths (System32\inetsrv, Microsoft.NET\Framework64) or modifications to applicationHost.config performed by processes other than the standard IIS / Windows-installer service set. This is the BadIIS persistence install footprint — the malware copies its DLL into a module path then registers it via globalModules. Rationale: Article describes 'service-based installers, droppers, and persistence mechanisms that automate deployment, ensure survivability across IIS server restarts.' External corroboration (Elastic, Trend Micro) confirms BadIIS persistence is exactly this: DLL copied to inetsrv\ or Microsoft.NET\Framework64\ + applicationHost.config edited to register the module. Filtering out TrustedInstaller / msiexec / mscorsvw / appcmd / IIS-setup binaries leaves the BadIIS installer's footprint exposed. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/badiis-to-the-bone-new-insights-to-global-seo-poisoning-campaign • https://www.welivesecurity.com/2021/08/06/anatomy-native-iis-malware/ • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/25/b/chinese-speaking-group-manipulates-seo-with-badiis.html
ATT&CKT1505.004 T1543.003

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has @"\inetsrv\" and FileName endswith ".dll")
    or (FolderPath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\" and FileName endswith ".dll")
    or (FolderPath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework\" and FileName endswith ".dll")
    or FileName =~ "applicationHost.config"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","mscorsvw.exe","iissetup.exe","appcmd.exe","WindowsAdminCenter.exe","WaAppAgent.exe","WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe","MsDeploy.exe","ngen.exe","setup.exe","trustedinstaller.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectFile = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","Created","Modified")
    | where (TargetFilePath has @"\inetsrv\" and TargetFileName endswith ".dll")
        or (TargetFilePath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\" and TargetFileName endswith ".dll")
        or (TargetFilePath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework\" and TargetFileName endswith ".dll")
        or TargetFileName =~ "applicationHost.config"
    | where ActingProcessName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","mscorsvw.exe","iissetup.exe","appcmd.exe","WindowsAdminCenter.exe","WaAppAgent.exe","WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe","MsDeploy.exe","ngen.exe","setup.exe")
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="FileEvent", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256;
let SuspectProcess = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName =~ "appcmd.exe"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install module","add module","/section:globalModules","/section:modules")
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="ProcessCreate", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName;
union SuspectFile, SuspectProcess
| order by TimeGenerated desc
